name: Northwest Couloir / Eldorado Glacier

pitch_detail.notes: Lower couloir, often simul-climbed; angle and ice quality vary by year/season.

pitch_detail.grade: AI2-3, up to WI3 in lean conditions
pitch_detail.notes: Upper couloir to the flat shoulder below the summit block; steepest, most sustained section.

rappels: Retreat possible via ice screw/picket rappels; alternate descent uses 2 rappels off the Eldorado/Dean's Tower notch
descent_text: From the summit, do not reverse the couloir — descend via the standard East Ridge / Inspiration Glacier route: downclimb the knife-edge summit ridge, drop through the gap in the lower East Ridge, rope up and cross the Inspiration Glacier, then descend the Eldorado Glacier back toward Roush Basin and Eldorado Creek Basin, finishing on the timbered climbers' trail back to the Cascade River crossing and trailhead (see the East Ridge route for full detail). This is a walk-off/downclimb with no rappels required on the descent itself — one party even skied the knife-edge ridge and glacier on the way down. Rappelling comes up on this route only on the approach/entry into the couloir, not on the summit descent: one party used a 40-meter rappel off the Inspiration Glacier side to drop into the couloir's gully system, anchored on two pitons with some newish tat, and noted a full 60m rope would get a party through everything in one rappel rather than needing to downclimb the remainder — but again, this is describing getting into the route, not descending from the summit. Because the descent is the shared East Ridge walk-off, treat glacier crevasse hazard and knife-edge icing exactly as on that route, and carry a rope for the glacier crossings regardless of whether any rappelling was used higher on the mountain.
approach: Same trailhead and lower approach as the East Ridge: Eldorado Trailhead at Cascade River Road mile 20 (~2,100 ft), cross the Cascade River via the log/three-tree crossing about 90 ft downstream of the parking area, then climb the steep timbered climbers' trail into a dry boulderfield (roughly to 4,500 ft) and on into Eldorado Creek Basin. From there, continue as for the East Ridge over the Roush Divide and up the Eldorado Glacier, then trend toward the Eldorado–Dean's Spire col on the mountain's northwest side to reach the wild Marble Creek Cirque, with views of Dorado Needle and Early Morning Spire. The approach to this face is longer and more involved than the East Ridge approach — a long, somewhat complicated route across glaciated and crevassed terrain, so rope up for the glacier sections. High camp is typically established either in Eldorado Creek/Roush Creek Basin or higher at the Eldorado-Inspiration Glacier site (~7,500–7,600 ft). One recorded ascent (climbing from the trailhead in a single push) took roughly 5 hours to reach the couloir's base; that party also used a shortcut of a belayed downclimb (~35 m) and two 30-meter rappels down a snow/rock gully near the Eldorado–Dean's Spire col to drop directly to within about 100 yards of the couloir, which meaningfully shortens the standard glacier traverse but is a variation, not the only way in — most parties simply continue glacier travel around to the couloir's base at about 7,800 ft. Hazards on approach: crevasses on the Eldorado/Inspiration Glaciers, a long featureless glacier crossing that can be disorienting in whiteout, and the optional gully downclimb/rappel shortcut is itself exposed snow-and-rock terrain.
overview: The Northwest Ice Couloir splits the northwest face of Eldorado above the wild Marble Creek Cirque, offering 2-3 long pitches (often simul-climbed) up the couloir to a flat shoulder just below the summit's famous knife-edge ridge — a steeper, more technical alternative to the standard East Ridge, reached via a long and fairly complex glaciated traverse around the mountain.
beta: Approach via the East Ridge glacier track to a rappel notch between Eldorado Peak and Dean's Spire (~8,100 ft), rappel into the west-facing cirque, then climb the couloir (~1,000 ft, 7,800–8,800 ft) on snow, neve, or ice depending on conditions — steps to 70–80° — to join the upper East Ridge.
gear: 5-6 ice screws, including a couple of stubbies
light rock rack to about 2 in, with a few pitons useful for belay anchors
70m rope for full-length rappels on descent (a 60m works but needs an extra rappel)
